analysis.assessment: LAB-0225 is a newly available (2024-12-01T12:00:00Z, the investigation cutoff) action-level relative_bioburden_signal result on an upstream process sample from BATCH-075 (Famotidine Injection, USP, LINE-A, started 06:40Z, still in production with no disposition): 1.23 action-limit ratio versus action limit 1.0 and alert limit 0.7, i.e. 123.0% of its action limit, status 'action', sample collected 10:40Z. It is the highest bioburden-signal result recorded in the scoped package. A paired sample five minutes later (PRE-LAB-001, 10:45Z) reads 0.79 (alert level). Scope: within the package, only two historical results also reached the action limit - LAB-0010 (SYN-0004, 1.08, status action; batch released after review) and LAB-0043 (SYN-0014, 1.06, invalidated after a resample read 0.22 normal; batch released); six further batches show alert-range historical results; no other batch shows an action-level result on 2024-12-01. The co-observed environmental monitoring result EM-0075 (process support area, 10:50Z) is marginally above its alert limit (0.71 vs 0.7, status alert); the four BATCH-075 historian process events (08:40-11:10Z) are all within expected ranges; the operator check (07:55Z) is normal; no deviation references BATCH-075, and the maintenance record shows only planned VESSEL-01 inspections (latest 2024-10-25, consistent with the recorded 6-7 week cadence) with no work order for PUMP-02 or AREA-CORE anywhere in scope. Plausible explanations remain open: a true bioburden excursion (H-1), a sampling/analytical artifact on the 10:40 sample (H-2, supported by the site's own repeat-and-invalidate precedent), an area/equipment contribution (H-3, weakly supported by the marginal EM alert), or a recording error (H-4, least supported). The scoped package cannot discriminate between H-1 and H-2: no assay replicates, sampling SOP or QA review record for LAB-0225 exist in scope, and the result became available exactly at the cutoff, so no review decision can exist yet. Human-reviewed next steps (advisory; this investigation approves and executes nothing): laboratory review of LAB-0225 with a repeat/resample decision following the site's own precedent; hold the BATCH-075 disposition until that review concludes; environmental and equipment checks for the process support area. Proposed severity MEDIUM: an in-process (not finished-product) action-level excursion on the package's highest recorded value, with a paired alert-level result, in-range process parameters and historical precedent of resolution via review. Final severity is determined by the configured routing policy, not by this proposal. Report type partial_investigation: two scoped sources - the image-only scanned laboratory review PDF and the JSON package manifest - were read in full/sampled but their text cells cannot be re-transcribed by the available source verifier, so their citations remain explicitly pending human source verification; their content is excluded from the certified claim ledger and disclosed in the coverage dispositions and synthesis. All other coverage (screening units, priority candidates), claims, arithmetic and temporal ordering are complete and machine-verified.

draft_report.assessment: LAB-0225 is a newly available (2024-12-01T12:00:00Z, the investigation cutoff) action-level relative_bioburden_signal result on an upstream process sample from BATCH-075 (Famotidine Injection, USP, LINE-A, started 06:40Z, still in production with no disposition): 1.23 action-limit ratio versus action limit 1.0 and alert limit 0.7, i.e. 123.0% of its action limit, status 'action', sample collected 10:40Z. It is the highest bioburden-signal result recorded in the scoped package. A paired sample five minutes later (PRE-LAB-001, 10:45Z) reads 0.79 (alert level). Scope: within the package, only two historical results also reached the action limit - LAB-0010 (SYN-0004, 1.08, status action; batch released after review) and LAB-0043 (SYN-0014, 1.06, invalidated after a resample read 0.22 normal; batch released); six further batches show alert-range historical results; no other batch shows an action-level result on 2024-12-01. The co-observed environmental monitoring result EM-0075 (process support area, 10:50Z) is marginally above its alert limit (0.71 vs 0.7, status alert); the four BATCH-075 historian process events (08:40-11:10Z) are all within expected ranges; the operator check (07:55Z) is normal; no deviation references BATCH-075, and the maintenance record shows only planned VESSEL-01 inspections (latest 2024-10-25, consistent with the recorded 6-7 week cadence) with no work order for PUMP-02 or AREA-CORE anywhere in scope. Plausible explanations remain open: a true bioburden excursion (H-1), a sampling/analytical artifact on the 10:40 sample (H-2, supported by the site's own repeat-and-invalidate precedent), an area/equipment contribution (H-3, weakly supported by the marginal EM alert), or a recording error (H-4, least supported). The scoped package cannot discriminate between H-1 and H-2: no assay replicates, sampling SOP or QA review record for LAB-0225 exist in scope, and the result became available exactly at the cutoff, so no review decision can exist yet. Human-reviewed next steps (advisory; this investigation approves and executes nothing): laboratory review of LAB-0225 with a repeat/resample decision following the site's own precedent; hold the BATCH-075 disposition until that review concludes; environmental and equipment checks for the process support area. Proposed severity MEDIUM: an in-process (not finished-product) action-level excursion on the package's highest recorded value, with a paired alert-level result, in-range process parameters and historical precedent of resolution via review. Final severity is determined by the configured routing policy, not by this proposal. Report type partial_investigation: two scoped sources - the image-only scanned laboratory review PDF and the JSON package manifest - were read in full/sampled but their text cells cannot be re-transcribed by the available source verifier, so their citations remain explicitly pending human source verification; their content is excluded from the certified claim ledger and disclosed in the coverage dispositions and synthesis. draft_report.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared patterns: (1) The laboratory evidence for LAB-0225 is internally consistent across four exports of one underlying record set - lims_export.csv, microbiology_results.xlsx (identical partition manifest), lims_review_local.csv (UTC-07 local-time alias, 123.0 % of limit via the manifest ratio_rule) and scanned_lab_review.pdf (OCR duplicate) - so consistency is transcription consistency, not independent confirmation. (2) The package shows a repeating same-day pairing of an elevated upstream bioburden result with an alert-level paired result five minutes later (BATCH-075: LAB-0225 1.23 action at 10:40Z with PRE-LAB-001 0.79 alert at 10:45Z; SYN-0004: LAB-0010 1.08 action at 11:00Z with PRE-LAB-004 0.88 alert at 11:05Z), and a repeat-and-invalidate precedent (SYN-0014: LAB-0043 1.06 invalidated, resample LAB-0044 0.22 normal) - both historical batches were later released. (3) Environmental and product-side microbial signals co-occur: the three historical batches with above-alert environmental monitoring results (SYN-0018 0.7743, SYN-0029 0.8183, SYN-0032 0.8111) are the same batches that carry above-alert bioburden results (0.7829, 0.8597, 0.8396), and BATCH-075 now shows the same pairing (EM-0075 0.71 alert with LAB-0225 1.23 action), though no causal direction is established. (4) All 12 deterministic priority candidates were reviewed: 11 clock-quality flags are time-basis ingestion artifacts (explicit timestamps present, parsed time_basis unresolved) and the paired recurrence-flag comparison is a screening artifact over two expected zeros; none corresponds to an out-of-range process value. Exceptions and gaps: the single out-of-range historian value package-wide is SYN-0015/PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs expected high 1.1 (severity 'high', 2024-04-05) with no deviation, CAPA or work-order follow-up recorded anywhere in scope, and no maintenance record exists for PUMP-02 or AREA-CORE at all; lims row 171 (LAB-0171, SYN-0057) has status 'missing' with no numerical result value and no follow-up row; BATCH-075 has no sterility/finished-product row yet (consistent with a batch still in production: start 06:40Z, no end-time, disposition or status cells); no deviation references BATCH-075 as of the cutoff. Missing evidence that bounds all conclusions: no assay replicates or precision data, no sampling SOP defining the PRE-LAB convention, no specification limit for the upstream bioburden-signal test, no QA review record for LAB-0225, and parsed process clocks unresolved for the cited rows (record-timestamp chronology only). Provenance: every examined row carries 'synthetic_factory_signal' and the deviations source marks its records as synthetic, so findings describe the scoped evidence package. Source-verification limits: the scanned laboratory review (image-only PDF) and the package manifest (JSON line records) cannot be re-transcribed by the available source verifier, so their content is reported here as read-but-not-machine-verified context and excluded from the certified claim ledger. Coverage: all screening units carry completed review dispositions; process_event_points.pdf was read to the end of file and its event lines mirror the fully analyzed historian events one-for-one.

interpretations.statement: Under the source's own limit structure, LAB-0225 requires action-level laboratory review: 1.23 exceeds the 1.0 action limit (123.0% of it) and the 0.7 alert limit. This is an advisory interpretation; the site's action procedure governs.

The two BATCH-075 samples taken five minutes apart differ materially (difference and percent change per the linked metrics, with rounding per the declared display decimals). The scoped package contains no replicate, precision or sampling-SOP data, so this gap cannot be classified as expected analytical variability versus a real change; it keeps both a true-excursion and an artifact explanation open.

analysis.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared patterns: (1) The laboratory evidence for LAB-0225 is internally consistent across four exports of one underlying record set - lims_export.csv, microbiology_results.xlsx (identical partition manifest), lims_review_local.csv (UTC-07 local-time alias, 123.0 % of limit via the manifest ratio_rule) and scanned_lab_review.pdf (OCR duplicate) - so consistency is transcription consistency, not independent confirmation. (2) The package shows a repeating same-day pairing of an elevated upstream bioburden result with an alert-level paired result five minutes later (BATCH-075: LAB-0225 1.23 action at 10:40Z with PRE-LAB-001 0.79 alert at 10:45Z; SYN-0004: LAB-0010 1.08 action at 11:00Z with PRE-LAB-004 0.88 alert at 11:05Z), and a repeat-and-invalidate precedent (SYN-0014: LAB-0043 1.06 invalidated, resample LAB-0044 0.22 normal) - both historical batches were later released. (3) Environmental and product-side microbial signals co-occur: the three historical batches with above-alert environmental monitoring results (SYN-0018 0.7743, SYN-0029 0.8183, SYN-0032 0.8111) are the same batches that carry above-alert bioburden results (0.7829, 0.8597, 0.8396), and BATCH-075 now shows the same pairing (EM-0075 0.71 alert with LAB-0225 1.23 action), though no causal direction is established. (4) All 12 deterministic priority candidates were reviewed: 11 clock-quality flags are time-basis ingestion artifacts (explicit timestamps present, parsed time_basis unresolved) and the paired recurrence-flag comparison is a screening artifact over two expected zeros; none corresponds to an out-of-range process value. Exceptions and gaps: the single out-of-range historian value package-wide is SYN-0015/PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs expected high 1.1 (severity 'high', 2024-04-05) with no deviation, CAPA or work-order follow-up recorded anywhere in scope, and no maintenance record exists for PUMP-02 or AREA-CORE at all; lims row 171 (LAB-0171, SYN-0057) has status 'missing' with no numerical result value and no follow-up row; BATCH-075 has no sterility/finished-product row yet (consistent with a batch still in production: start 06:40Z, no end-time, disposition or status cells); no deviation references BATCH-075 as of the cutoff. Missing evidence that bounds all conclusions: no assay replicates or precision data, no sampling SOP defining the PRE-LAB convention, no specification limit for the upstream bioburden-signal test, no QA review record for LAB-0225, and parsed process clocks unresolved for the cited rows (record-timestamp chronology only). Provenance: every examined row carries 'synthetic_factory_signal' and the deviations source marks its records as synthetic, so findings describe the scoped evidence package. Source-verification limits: the scanned laboratory review (image-only PDF) and the package manifest (JSON line records) cannot be re-transcribed by the available source verifier, so their content is reported here as read-but-not-machine-verified context and excluded from the certified claim ledger. Coverage: all screening units carry completed review dispositions; process_event_points.pdf was read to the end of file and its event lines mirror the fully analyzed historian events one-for-one.

interpretations.statement: Under the source's own limit structure, LAB-0225 requires action-level laboratory review: 1.23 exceeds the 1.0 action limit (123.0% of it) and the 0.7 alert limit. This is an advisory interpretation; the site's action procedure governs.

The two BATCH-075 samples taken five minutes apart differ materially (difference and percent change per the linked metrics, with rounding per the declared display decimals). The scoped package contains no replicate, precision or sampling-SOP data, so this gap cannot be classified as expected analytical variability versus a real change; it keeps both a true-excursion and an artifact explanation open.

The recorded process evidence for BATCH-075 on 2024-12-01 (four in-range historian events, one normal operator check) does not show a process excursion; however, discrete event points cannot exclude a localized bioburden cause, and temporal association alone cannot support causation.

LAB-0225 became available exactly at the investigation cutoff (2024-12-01T12:00:00Z), so no laboratory review decision, invalidation record or repeat result for it can exist inside the scoped package; the review is necessarily a next step, not a completed step.

The missing_source_time flags on all priority candidates are acquisition/time-basis artifacts, not missing timestamps and not process faults: every flagged record carries explicit timestamp cells (historian timestamp/occurred_at; laboratory sample_collected_at/occurred_at/available_at; lims_review_local timezone-qualified 'Released local (UTC-07)'), but the pipeline marks time_basis='unresolved' on these cells.

The recurrence_flag paired comparison (candidate ab4255eaafcbc848caa3, both peaks 0.0) is a screening artifact: recurrence_flag 0 is the expected no-recurrence value for these closed, low-severity, procedure-category deviations, so the descriptive zero-vs-zero comparison flag is not a material process signal.

Values within expected ranges for the historian candidates (SYN-0011, SYN-0028, BATCH-075) show the clock-quality flags do not correspond to out-of-range process values; the single historian out-of-range value (SYN-0015) was not flagged by screening as a priority candidate.

Alert-band bioburden results for SYN-0018, SYN-0032 and SYN-0029 (values per the cited result cells) are recorded in their sources with status 'alert' (above their alert limit, below the action limit); these are source-acknowledged alert endpoints, distinct from the clock flags and not by themselves action-limit exceedances.

The BATCH-075 review record (123.0% of action limit, review status 'action', released at the as-of instant) is the most material observation among the reviewed candidates. A separate same-morning BATCH-075 in-process record (PRE-LAB-001, 0.79 action-limit ratio, status 'alert') is below the action limit, so the two records are not numerically consistent as measurements of the same quantity; their relationship is unresolved.

The process_event_points.pdf note 'Each point is one recorded event. No continuous trajectory is inferred.' constrains process-clock interpretation: historian and process-event source points must not be treated as continuous process trajectories.

The EM-0075 record independently corroborates an alert-level (not action-level) environmental microbial signal for BATCH-075 on the same production day as the action-level LAB-0225 result. The two measurements agree in direction but differ in magnitude and limit category (EM 0.71 vs alert 0.7; LAB 1.23 vs action 1.0 per lead-provided context and lab screening anchors). EM is an environmental measurement, not a product assay; temporal proximity does not establish a shared cause.

Above-alert EM values have historical precedent in this file: three batches in the April-to-June period of the production year recorded higher EM results than BATCH-075 (values per the cited result cells), all classified 'alert', none reaching the action limit. BATCH-075's EM value is the lowest of the four above-alert values; whether those historical batches had comparable lab results was not established by this read.

The recorded maintenance pattern (six closed planned inspections on VESSEL-01 at roughly six-to-seven-week intervals, latest 2024-10-25) means the absence of a November work order is consistent with the established cadence; it is not evidence that maintenance was missed, nor that equipment condition was good. No work order exists for PUMP-02 or AREA-CORE anywhere in these two sources - a coverage gap about where (or whether) their maintenance is recorded, not proof that no maintenance occurred.

No deviation references BATCH-075 as of the 2024-12-01T12:00:00Z cutoff, while the lead-provided LAB-0225 sample was collected at 10:40 the same morning. Given the result only became available near the cutoff, the absence is consistent with a deviation not yet opened; it is a timing observation, not proof of either a QA gap or process failure.

The BATCH-075 batch record carries no end-time, disposition, status or first-ship-time cells in the returned row. With start 2024-12-01T06:40:00Z and the cutoff at 12:00:00Z the same day, this is consistent with a batch still in progress, but record incompleteness cannot be distinguished from in-progress status using the returned cells alone.

Every cell read this run from batch_records, environmental_monitoring, both maintenance sources and deviations carries provenance value 'synthetic_factory_signal'; the package is synthetic demonstration data, so findings describe the evidence package contents rather than a real manufacturing event.

Question A answer: LAB-0225 is not the only action-level laboratory result in the scoped package. LAB-0010 (SYN-0004, result 1.08, 2024-02-21) also carries status 'action' in lims_export.csv, microbiology_results.xlsx and lims_review_local.csv. LAB-0225 is, however, the only action-level result for BATCH-075 and the only one dated 2024-12-01; LAB-0043 (1.06) exceeds its action limit but is marked 'invalidated' (repeat sample), so the source treats it as not effective.

Question B answer: microbiology_results.xlsx appears to duplicate lims_export.csv. The sampled PRE-LAB-003, PRE-LAB-001 and LAB-0225 records are identical on result_id, batch, value, status and timestamps; in a row-by-row comparison of the two full numeric projections (all rows with numeric cells, no truncation) no differing entity or value was found; analysis-preparation metadata records identical partition manifest digests for the two sources. Text cells were compared only on the sampled records.

Question C answer: PRE-LAB-001 (0.79, alert) and LAB-0225 (1.23, action) are two BATCH-075 results from upstream process samples collected five minutes apart (10:40Z and 10:45Z), with the lower result released earlier (11:15Z) than the higher one (12:00Z). The 'PRE-LAB-' prefix is not unique to BATCH-075 (PRE-LAB-003 on SYN-0001, PRE-LAB-004 on SYN-0004), and no scoped source defines what the prefix means; PRE-LAB-002 did not appear in my searches (not proof of absence). The two results are discordant relative to the 1.0 action limit.

Question D answer: lims_review_local.csv is a local-time (UTC-07) aliased review export of the same laboratory records as lims_export.csv: Record mirrors result_id, Result (% of limit) mirrors numerical_result expressed as percent of the action limit (PRE-LAB-003 0.85 vs 85.0; LAB-0225 1.23 vs 123.0), Review status mirrors status (alert/action), and Released local (UTC-07) mirrors available_at shifted to UTC-07. The LAB-0111 record (SYN-0037) shows 7.57% of the action limit with Review status 'normal' - the screening anchor is the low extreme of the result series, not an excursion.

Beyond BATCH-075, the export contains alert-band results (at or above the alert limit and below the action limit) for PRE-LAB-003 (0.85), PRE-LAB-004 (0.88), a SYN-0014 bioburden result (0.8974), SYN-0015 (0.7862), SYN-0018 (0.7829), SYN-0029 (0.8597), SYN-0032 (0.8396) and SYN-0036 (0.7751); these are historical except PRE-LAB-001. All other results with numeric values are below the alert limit, and no result exceeds its specification_limit where one is stated.

BATCH-075 has only its two laboratory records in the export, while examined SYN batches also carry a sterility/finished-product record; the last such record (LAB-0215, SYN-0071) was collected 2024-11-15 and released 2024-11-29. A BATCH-075 sterility result collected 2024-12-01 would plausibly be released after the as_of cutoff, but this timing inference is unverified, and records without numeric cells were not attributed to batches in this review except LAB-0003 and LAB-0215.

The historian_export.csv and process_event_points.pdf search matches for the LAB-0225 identifier are PROC-0225 process events for SYN-0057, not references to the laboratory result; in the FTS search no deviation or operator-event mention of LAB-0225 was returned.

workflow.assessment: LAB-0225 is a newly available (2024-12-01T12:00:00Z, the investigation cutoff) action-level relative_bioburden_signal result on an upstream process sample from BATCH-075 (Famotidine Injection, USP, LINE-A, started 06:40Z, still in production with no disposition): 1.23 action-limit ratio versus action limit 1.0 and alert limit 0.7, i.e. 123.0% of its action limit, status 'action', sample collected 10:40Z. It is the highest bioburden-signal result recorded in the scoped package. A paired sample five minutes later (PRE-LAB-001, 10:45Z) reads 0.79 (alert level). Scope: within the package, only two historical results also reached the action limit - LAB-0010 (SYN-0004, 1.08, status action; batch released after review) and LAB-0043 (SYN-0014, 1.06, invalidated after a resample read 0.22 normal; batch released); six further batches show alert-range historical results; no other batch shows an action-level result on 2024-12-01. The co-observed environmental monitoring result EM-0075 (process support area, 10:50Z) is marginally above its alert limit (0.71 vs 0.7, status alert); the four BATCH-075 historian process events (08:40-11:10Z) are all within expected ranges; the operator check (07:55Z) is normal; no deviation references BATCH-075, and the maintenance record shows only planned VESSEL-01 inspections (latest 2024-10-25, consistent with the recorded 6-7 week cadence) with no work order for PUMP-02 or AREA-CORE anywhere in scope. Plausible explanations remain open: a true bioburden excursion (H-1), a sampling/analytical artifact on the 10:40 sample (H-2, supported by the site's own repeat-and-invalidate precedent), an area/equipment contribution (H-3, weakly supported by the marginal EM alert), or a recording error (H-4, least supported). Human-reviewed next steps (advisory; this investigation approves and executes nothing): laboratory review of LAB-0225 with a repeat/resample decision following the site's own precedent; hold the BATCH-075 disposition until that review concludes; environmental and equipment checks for the process support area. Proposed severity MEDIUM: an in-process (not finished-product) action-level excursion on the package's highest recorded value, with a paired alert-level result, in-range process parameters and historical precedent of resolution via review. Final severity is determined by the configured routing policy, not by this proposal. (2) The package shows a repeating same-day pairing of an elevated upstream bioburden result with an alert-level paired result five minutes later (BATCH-075: LAB-0225 1.23 action at 10:40Z with PRE-LAB-001 0.79 alert at 10:45Z; SYN-0004: LAB-0010 1.08 action at 11:00Z with PRE-LAB-004 0.88 alert at 11:05Z), and a repeat-and-invalidate precedent (SYN-0014: LAB-0043 1.06 invalidated, resample LAB-0044 0.22 normal) - both historical batches were later released. (3) Environmental and product-side microbial signals co-occur: the three historical batches with above-alert environmental monitoring results (SYN-0018 0.7743, SYN-0029 0.8183, SYN-0032 0.8111) are the same batches that carry above-alert bioburden results (0.7829, 0.8597, 0.8396), and BATCH-075 now shows the same pairing (EM-0075 0.71 alert with LAB-0225 1.23 action), though no causal direction is established. (4) All 12 deterministic priority candidates were reviewed: 11 clock-quality flags are time-basis ingestion artifacts (explicit timestamps present, parsed time_basis unresolved) and the paired recurrence-flag comparison is a screening artifact over two expected zeros; none corresponds to an out-of-range process value. Exceptions and gaps: the single out-of-range historian value package-wide is SYN-0015/PUMP-02 equipment_pressure_ratio 1.24 vs expected high 1.1 (severity 'high', 2024-04-05) with no deviation, CAPA or work-order follow-up recorded anywhere in scope, and no maintenance record exists for PUMP-02 or AREA-CORE at all; lims row 171 (LAB-0171, SYN-0057) has status 'missing' with no numerical result value and no follow-up row; BATCH-075 has no sterility/finished-product row yet (consistent with a batch still in production: start 06:40Z, no end-time, disposition or status cells); no deviation references BATCH-075 as of the cutoff. Missing evidence that bounds all conclusions: no assay replicates or precision data, no sampling SOP defining the PRE-LAB convention, no specification limit for the upstream bioburden-signal test, no QA review record for LAB-0225, and parsed process clocks unresolved for the cited rows (record-timestamp chronology only). Provenance: every examined row carries 'synthetic_factory_signal' and the deviations source marks its records as synthetic, so findings describe the scoped evidence package. Source-verification limits: the scanned laboratory review (image-only PDF) and the package manifest (JSON line records) cannot be re-transcribed by the available source verifier, so their content is reported here as read-but-not-machine-verified context and excluded from the certified claim ledger. Coverage: all screening units carry completed review dispositions; process_event_points.pdf was read to the end of file and its event lines mirror the fully analyzed historian events one-for-one.

interpretations.statement: Under the source's own limit structure, LAB-0225 requires action-level laboratory review: 1.23 exceeds the 1.0 action limit (123.0% of it) and the 0.7 alert limit. This is an advisory interpretation; the site's action procedure governs.

The two BATCH-075 samples taken five minutes apart differ materially (difference and percent change per the linked metrics, with rounding per the declared display decimals). The scoped package contains no replicate, precision or sampling-SOP data, so this gap cannot be classified as expected analytical variability versus a real change; it keeps both a true-excursion and an artifact explanation open.

The recorded process evidence for BATCH-075 on 2024-12-01 (four in-range historian events, one normal operator check) does not show a process excursion; however, discrete event points cannot exclude a localized bioburden cause, and temporal association alone cannot support causation.

LAB-0225 became available exactly at the investigation cutoff (2024-12-01T12:00:00Z), so no laboratory review decision, invalidation record or repeat result for it can exist inside the scoped package; the review is necessarily a next step, not a completed step.

The missing_source_time flags on all priority candidates are acquisition/time-basis artifacts, not missing timestamps and not process faults: every flagged record carries explicit timestamp cells (historian timestamp/occurred_at; laboratory sample_collected_at/occurred_at/available_at; lims_review_local timezone-qualified 'Released local (UTC-07)'), but the pipeline marks time_basis='unresolved' on these cells.

The recurrence_flag paired comparison (candidate ab4255eaafcbc848caa3, both peaks 0.0) is a screening artifact: recurrence_flag 0 is the expected no-recurrence value for these closed, low-severity, procedure-category deviations, so the descriptive zero-vs-zero comparison flag is not a material process signal.

Values within expected ranges for the historian candidates (SYN-0011, SYN-0028, BATCH-075) show the clock-quality flags do not correspond to out-of-range process values; the single historian out-of-range value (SYN-0015) was not flagged by screening as a priority candidate.

Alert-band bioburden results for SYN-0018, SYN-0032 and SYN-0029 (values per the cited result cells) are recorded in their sources with status 'alert' (above their alert limit, below the action limit); these are source-acknowledged alert endpoints, distinct from the clock flags and not by themselves action-limit exceedances.

The BATCH-075 review record (123.0% of action limit, review status 'action', released at the as-of instant) is the most material observation among the reviewed candidates. A separate same-morning BATCH-075 in-process record (PRE-LAB-001, 0.79 action-limit ratio, status 'alert') is below the action limit, so the two records are not numerically consistent as measurements of the same quantity; their relationship is unresolved.

The process_event_points.pdf note 'Each point is one recorded event. No continuous trajectory is inferred.' constrains process-clock interpretation: historian and process-event source points must not be treated as continuous process trajectories.

The EM-0075 record independently corroborates an alert-level (not action-level) environmental microbial signal for BATCH-075 on the same production day as the action-level LAB-0225 result. The two measurements agree in direction but differ in magnitude and limit category (EM 0.71 vs alert 0.7; LAB 1.23 vs action 1.0 per lead-provided context and lab screening anchors). EM is an environmental measurement, not a product assay; temporal proximity does not establish a shared cause.

Above-alert EM values have historical precedent in this file: three batches in the April-to-June period of the production year recorded higher EM results than BATCH-075 (values per the cited result cells), all classified 'alert', none reaching the action limit. BATCH-075's EM value is the lowest of the four above-alert values; whether those historical batches had comparable lab results was not established by this read.

The recorded maintenance pattern (six closed planned inspections on VESSEL-01 at roughly six-to-seven-week intervals, latest 2024-10-25) means the absence of a November work order is consistent with the established cadence; it is not evidence that maintenance was missed, nor that equipment condition was good. No work order exists for PUMP-02 or AREA-CORE anywhere in these two sources - a coverage gap about where (or whether) their maintenance is recorded, not proof that no maintenance occurred.

No deviation references BATCH-075 as of the 2024-12-01T12:00:00Z cutoff, while the lead-provided LAB-0225 sample was collected at 10:40 the same morning. Given the result only became available near the cutoff, the absence is consistent with a deviation not yet opened; it is a timing observation, not proof of either a QA gap or process failure.

The BATCH-075 batch record carries no end-time, disposition, status or first-ship-time cells in the returned row. With start 2024-12-01T06:40:00Z and the cutoff at 12:00:00Z the same day, this is consistent with a batch still in progress, but record incompleteness cannot be distinguished from in-progress status using the returned cells alone.

Every cell read this run from batch_records, environmental_monitoring, both maintenance sources and deviations carries provenance value 'synthetic_factory_signal'; the package is synthetic demonstration data, so findings describe the evidence package contents rather than a real manufacturing event.

Question A answer: LAB-0225 is not the only action-level laboratory result in the scoped package. LAB-0010 (SYN-0004, result 1.08, 2024-02-21) also carries status 'action' in lims_export.csv, microbiology_results.xlsx and lims_review_local.csv. LAB-0225 is, however, the only action-level result for BATCH-075 and the only one dated 2024-12-01; LAB-0043 (1.06) exceeds its action limit but is marked 'invalidated' (repeat sample), so the source treats it as not effective.

Question B answer: microbiology_results.xlsx appears to duplicate lims_export.csv. The sampled PRE-LAB-003, PRE-LAB-001 and LAB-0225 records are identical on result_id, batch, value, status and timestamps; in a row-by-row comparison of the two full numeric projections (all rows with numeric cells, no truncation) no differing entity or value was found; analysis-preparation metadata records identical partition manifest digests for the two sources. The 'PRE-LAB-' prefix is not unique to BATCH-075 (PRE-LAB-003 on SYN-0001, PRE-LAB-004 on SYN-0004), and no scoped source defines what the prefix means; PRE-LAB-002 did not appear in my searches (not proof of absence). The two results are discordant relative to the 1.0 action limit.

Question D answer: lims_review_local.csv is a local-time (UTC-07) aliased review export of the same laboratory records as lims_export.csv: Record mirrors result_id, Result (% of limit) mirrors numerical_result expressed as percent of the action limit (PRE-LAB-003 0.85 vs 85.0; LAB-0225 1.23 vs 123.0), Review status mirrors status (alert/action), and Released local (UTC-07) mirrors available_at shifted to UTC-07. The LAB-0111 record (SYN-0037) shows 7.57% of the action limit with Review status 'normal' - the screening anchor is the low extreme of the result series, not an excursion.

Beyond BATCH-075, the export contains alert-band results (at or above the alert limit and below the action limit) for PRE-LAB-003 (0.85), PRE-LAB-004 (0.88), a SYN-0014 bioburden result (0.8974), SYN-0015 (0.7862), SYN-0018 (0.7829), SYN-0029 (0.8597), SYN-0032 (0.8396) and SYN-0036 (0.7751); these are historical except PRE-LAB-001. All other results with numeric values are below the alert limit, and no result exceeds its specification_limit where one is stated.

BATCH-075 has only its two laboratory records in the export, while examined SYN batches also carry a sterility/finished-product record; the last such record (LAB-0215, SYN-0071) was collected 2024-11-15 and released 2024-11-29. A BATCH-075 sterility result collected 2024-12-01 would plausibly be released after the as_of cutoff, but this timing inference is unverified, and records without numeric cells were not attributed to batches in this review except LAB-0003 and LAB-0215.

The historian_export.csv and process_event_points.pdf search matches for the LAB-0225 identifier are PROC-0225 process events for SYN-0057, not references to the laboratory result; in the FTS search no deviation or operator-event mention of LAB-0225 was returned.
